Normal: Windows has promised most of what it can hand out. If this is normal for how you use the PC, check Task Manager > Details > 'Commit size' for the programs holding the most.
If one program keeps growing for hours (a browser, or dwm.exe after a graphics driver bug), restarting it or updating its driver usually fixes it.
Bad: Windows is close to its limit: at 100% programs crash or refuse to start, even if 'memory in use' looks moderate.
Close what you are not using, then check Task Manager > Details > 'Commit size' for the program holding the most.
A larger page file (or a second one on another drive) raises the limit at once; more RAM is the lasting fix if this is normal use.

rules.forecast: When the limit is reached Windows shows 'out of memory', and programs can close without saving.

Normal: Windows came close to running out of memory once this month. Worth noting what was open; if it happens again, see the tips for repeated warnings.
Bad: Windows ran out of memory more than once this month, and programs may have crashed because of it.
Event Viewer > Windows Logs > System, event 2004 (Resource-Exhaustion-Detector), names the programs using the most each time.
Common causes: a virtual machine or local AI model sized for more RAM than this PC has, many browser tabs, or a leaking program such as dwm.exe with an outdated graphics driver.
Raise the page-file limit (or add one on another drive) as a quick fix; add RAM if this is how the PC is normally used.
